method: A table procedure with one rule about the line, fitted on public paragraph text only. Every line has nine words. The first word of each line is drawn by frequency from the public words that begin with p or f; the other eight are drawn by frequency from all public words, with no regard to order (so p or f words turn up inside lines at their ordinary rate, 1.8%). Words are independent draws: no word order, no meaning. 2,600 lines, fixed seed, generated once, laid on the pages line by line (cut lines). The writer sees the start of a line and nothing else; it does not know where paragraphs begin. It still reproduces F-003, because a text in which every line opens with a gallows word also has every paragraph open with one. On the practice split the ratio is 58.5 against the manuscript's 54.6. Read with care: this shows that F-003 as specified does not separate a paragraph-opening habit from a line-opening one and needs no language; it does not show that the manuscript's lines open this way (they do not: the manuscript concentrates p and f on paragraph starts). A fact comparing paragraph-initial words with other line-initial words would not fall to this text.
